binary_provenance.dirty_describes: uncommitted TRACKED modifications in the worktree the BINARY was compiled from, at compile time
binary_provenance.note: Read out of the binary's own compiled-in build fingerprint (.rdata string literals stamped by cmake/GenerateBuildFingerprint.cmake). This is the only commit in this manifest that describes the code that ran.

source_worktree_head_at_capture.dirty_describes: 'dirty' here = uncommitted TRACKED modifications in the SOURCE WORKTREE at capture time. It says nothing about whether the measured binary was built from a clean tree; that is identity.binary_provenance.dirty.
source_worktree_head_at_capture.note: SOURCE WORKTREE HEAD at the moment this artifact was written. It does NOT describe the binary that was measured -- the tool's worktree and the worktree that compiled the exe are frequently different lanes. For the commit that was actually exercised, read identity.binary_provenance.

git.dirty_describes: 'dirty' here = uncommitted TRACKED modifications in the SOURCE WORKTREE at capture time. It says nothing about whether the measured binary was built from a clean tree; that is identity.binary_provenance.dirty.
git.note: SOURCE WORKTREE HEAD at the moment this artifact was written. It does NOT describe the binary that was measured -- the tool's worktree and the worktree that compiled the exe are frequently different lanes. For the commit that was actually exercised, read identity.binary_provenance.

binary_identity_established.detail: binary still on disk byte-identical; live re-read of its own stamp agrees: commit e9e3f19d6f6e (branch claude/lane2-s3, dirty=False).

binary_corroboration.note: Independent artifacts that record the SAME exe digest as identity.exe.sha256. Consumed by provenance_gate.establish() as W-ARTIFACT: each must still exist, still hash to `artifact_sha256`, and still name that digest. They are a convenience, not the only arm -- if these capture trees are pruned, W-REPO-COMMIT still corroborates from the git object database, which outlives every install.

source_worktree_head_at_bless.dirty_describes: 'dirty' here = uncommitted TRACKED modifications in the SOURCE WORKTREE at capture time. It says nothing about whether the measured binary was built from a clean tree; that is identity.binary_provenance.dirty.
source_worktree_head_at_bless.note: SOURCE WORKTREE HEAD of whoever ran bless.py. It does NOT describe the binary that rendered these crops -- the blessing worktree and the worktree that compiled the exe are routinely different lanes, and blessing can happen days after capture. For the commit that was actually exercised, read identity.binary_provenance.commit. This block exists only to find the lane that made the blessing decision.
